sentences.text: Hello?
Hello, Jason?
Yes, hi, how are you?
Good, how are you?
Are you phone calling or are you Google meeting?
Because I'll take my picture off.
Yeah, yeah, I'm in transit today, so I'm just calling by phone.
Okay, no worries.
And I don't have to look at myself either.
Fine, let me turn myself off there.
Okay, thanks for taking the time.

So you have, I mean this could be sort of a 10 minute call or it could go longer if it's interesting and you want to follow up, then we can get on the phone or zoom or whatever when you have a little bit more time.
You were responding to an outreach from Capital A, right, about a strategic acquisition?
That is correct, yes.
Okay, so I'll give you sort of a one second version and then we can decide where to go from there.
So I'm Heather Fullerton.
I work as a senior advisor at Capital A. I am not like an M and A person.
I worked in the advertising industry, creative production, all that for a very long time.
And I do this with Ann DJ at Capital A on the side when there's kind of interesting projects for me to find strategic matches for certain clients.

And one of our clients, I would say, who's focused more on, I would say Gen Z and now Gen Alpha are looking to acquire either completely aligned or complementary businesses that will help them build and grow, which will lead eventually to some kind of event over time.
But right now they're really looking for fast growth and you came up as an interesting area, you know, in terms of creator economy.
I would love to understand a bit more about your business, but they are looking to have a full acquisition and for that company to be part of their company.
And they are reputable, they are very good at what they do and well respected.
They're well funded and connected in order to be able to do this.
So I'll stop there for a second just because I know that's a lot of information and then we can get into more detail.
But I don't know much about your business other than I can find from the outside.
But I guess the question is, would you guys be open to entertaining this conversation?
Where are you and your growth and what questions can I answer from for you?
Sure, I think, I think we're, we're definitely open to entertaining the conversation a little bit more about, about myself and the company.
So I previously managed all the content, rights and licensing for Billboard magazine and Forbes.
That was about 15 years ago.
While I was in that industry.

I met up with an individual, his name was Joe Fernandez and at the time he owned company called Clout K L O U T. And he started telling me a little bit about what he was doing and after I left that meeting, decided that I was going to launch Higher Influence and as a result essentially created the groundwork for pioneering influencer marketing as a whole.
So influencer marketing did not exist when I launched Higher Influence in January of 2000, 2011.
Yeah, we were the very first into the space.
Very, very first into the space.
Nobody else was even close to existing Tap Influence at that time.
They were Blog Frog and they eventually migrated to influencer marketing.
They were second in line I think, but essentially we pioneered the full service influence marketing space.
Mondelez International was one of our very first clients and they're still a client today.
So they have Oreo, several other large brands underneath.
Funny, I worked for them way back in the day.
I worked for them and worked on Oreo in one of my agencies.
So I know them well.
Okay, right on.
Yeah, so they were one of our first clients.
Nobody had a clue what influencer marketing was back then.
So we, we grew slow, but we grew strong, we grew stable.
We built a very solid foundation, built our processes out of nothing.
You know, there, there wasn't any processes to follow.
And so we, we kind of paved our own path and today we are still doing the exact same thing.
Influencer marketing, marketing is all we've ever done.
We do it very well.
We do it for the largest brands in the world and we are probably one of the most award winning agencies that exist in the space.
With that said, again, we grew very slow.
We grew on a shoestring budget supporting our own growth.
We hadn't had any outside investor help in the past 10 years.
So we are self funded and I think the only loan we've ever.
What's that?
I'm sorry, That's a good place to be.
Self funded.
Yeah, yeah, exactly.
The only loan we've ever taken I think was, it was 180,000 or $200,000 loan during COVID Yeah, we took one of the Eidl loans, but it was for a minimal amount.
I think we're over halfway done with paying that off.
So we're essentially debt free.
Other than that we've got a team of around 15 that's contractors and employees.
We're not a huge agency.
We don't, it's not like we're knocking it out of the park and revenue, but we do, we're steady growth.
This year we're on track.
We should do five and a half to six million in sales in 2025.
So that kind of tells you where we're at.
Yeah, that's a good place to be for these guys.
And how are you?
So what would you say your kind of expected year on year growth is?
I know you said you've been sort of managing a slow steady growth but what are you guys looking at from like last year to this year and this year to next?
Do you have a sense?
Yeah.
So last year we ended up doing 5.1 million in sales.

But Match Group, which was one of our major clients, they had signed a three million dollar contract with us and they made it through their first million and said we don't have the budget to continue.
What do we do?
And we ended up dissolving that contract.
So we got shorted out of about 2 million in revenue because Match Group backed out of their contract.
So if you figure that we did, if you take away the 2 million, we only did 3, 3.2 million in sales and this year we'll do 5.5 to 6.
Yeah, so we'll double the sales of last year.
But another big exciting thing that we have going on, we have designed, developed all the UI UX is complete for an AI, a first to market.
Nothing like this exists.
It's an AI sentiment analysis platform for marketing projects of all type of social marketing projects.
It's not just influencer marketing but it's sentiment tracking on a SaaS level and this project is ready.
We should greenlight development within the next 30 days.
Like I said, the UI and UX is 100% complete.
We've spent the last three to four months working through that.
It's an incredible product.
I think it's, it's really going to fill a major void in the market and we're super stoked about it.
It's.
We've taken our 15 years of influencer marketing expertise and put it into this kind of building this platform from the ground up and it really is something spectacular.
So hoping to have that officially launched and off the ground by end of January 2026.
So that should be in full production by, by that point.
And that'll be a SaaS model so you'll have like a subscription.
It's a subscription model for any client.
Or is it only.
Is it complem your influencer work with your clients or is it anyone could use this just based on subscribing to it?
No, this is going to be an all out open use platform.
So filling a major void in the market for Sentiment analysis.
AI driven sentiment analysis for social marketing projects.
Yeah.
Nothing like it exists.
And so this will be on a subscription basis to anyone in the industry.
It can be used by brands that are working on internal social marketing projects.
It can be white labeled.
Yeah.
Different, different subscription tiers.
So we're very excited about that.
We were considering doing.
Sound like a good idea?
Yeah, yeah.
And anyone that sees these, these screenshots of what it's going to be will truly understand the potential of what we're holding in our hands right now.
Yeah.
Love to see it.
My other business in the AI world of things, so that's always fascinating.
Oh, okay.
Just something that I'm very, I'm very AI savvy, let's put it that way.
So.
And AI forward.
Gotcha.
So I appreciate it.

So that would be our move if we acquire the funding rather than going the M and A route.
And are you currently, are you currently raising funds or that's what you're going to do next or are you doing it right?
As we speak, we're putting together a pitch deck as we speak.
Okay.
And that would be to support, so the pitch deck would be to support technology, that this technology side of things, your SaaS business and to acquire a talent representation.
Is that right?
Is that what you said?
Correct?
A talent agency?
Yes, an established talent agency with 40 plus influencers on the roster.
And then we would just continue to build upon that based on our existing 15 year relationships.
Yeah.
So we're, we're fairly confident.
I don't know if these guys would do that.
They're not in the business of funding but you know, you know, in, in the scope of what they're looking at.
They could also be looking at talent.
We just put that as a secondary.
But they could be looking at talent agents as well.

But it's not just, you know, not just inquiring, acquiring influencers, but that could be something that could be on the, that could, that could quite nicely align with their next step strategies as well.
Let me ask you something because it's, it is.
So it sounds like you're in the right ballpark in terms of size and growth and ambition.
I think it's great that you have this new tool.

We work off of relationships that we have with other agencies.
That's why we want to acquire an internal one.
So, so really we're, we're wide open.
We don't have a single focus in terms of like a Gen X or you know, Gen Z or anything like that.
We, we're primarily a brand driven company.
So brands come to us for strategies and we build the strategy and develop.
We, we begin outreach to the influencers that perfectly align with the game plan.
Yeah, so yeah, they're all built.
In a way like strategy.
But I guess my question is.
Sorry, I wasn't clear.

My question is in that instance, in your current work, not the, not the agent or talent world, but in your current work, your brands obviously Mondelez and Oreo, I can say that's targeted sort of younger plus moms or something like that, what would you say the majority of your clients target audiences are?
I guess that's more where I'm headed.
Okay, gotcha.
Gotcha.
Yeah, so I would say toward the younger audiences because we're, we're dealing a lot with entertainment brands, with fashion and beauty brands, travel brands.
So a lot of the technology brands, a lot of what we're focusing on, the target audience does trend much younger.
Okay, that's helpful.
Okay, well, I do just based on this preliminary conversation, I do think you're actually quite an interesting fit for these guys.

What would be helpful for me to understand and looking at your site are you, would you say that you're more just understanding the capabilities, you're more service oriented, more services oriented than until your technology comes up then tech oriented.
It's not, you're not just a platform.
You're actually providing the strategy, the outreach to the influencers, the helping create the campaigns.
Is that.
Or create the content that's going to be developed with the, with the influencer or how would you describe the bulk of what you guys have been doing to date?
Yes.
So we are an extremely white glove service company.
So we cater to the biggest of the biggest in terms of brand relationships, brand partnerships.
And with that comes an unparalleled level of Service and experience.
So I would say that that's where our strengths really lie.
And, and what sets us apart from the field is, yeah, 15 years in the industry.
I mean essentially paving the road for all the other agencies that exist out there currently.
White glove, making sure that every attention to detail is checked.
That's what we bring to the table.
The, the majority of our team has been here for.
They don't.
There's not a revolving door here.
A lot of our team members have been here three, four, five, six years.
I'd say close to half of our team has been here for an extended period of time and the others just coming on board due to growth.
So our team is established, they've worked together for a long time.
They know the industry.
We're no, no amateurs involved.
But yes, we're, we're 100% service based until our technology platform Centrac rolls out.
And what kind of talent do you.
So you're mentioning that the people who've been there for a while are they strategists, account kind of managerish people.
Like what's the, what's the breakdown of your.
Would you say like 15 something?
Yes.
So we have, we have someone that's dedicated to all paid media and performance which would be reports, analytics.
He's got one individual underneath him.
We've got multiple campaign managers, we call them campaign success managers.
We've got a full time designer, we've got full time, I say full time, 30 hours a week, financial finance director.
We've got an HR manager in place.
We've got SlimMet, focuses on FCO.
That's another very interesting piece about us is we have zero outbound sales or marketing efforts.
Just about every bit of business we have is either repeat or incoming.
Yeah, good for you.
The only marketing we do is we've got an organic SEO person in place.
So we've got really high organic first page rankings for all the major keywords and we do run a very minimal pay per click in the background.
But no outbound sales, nothing like that.
It's, it's recently just been a revolving door of opportunity.
Yeah.
Okay.
And in terms of ownership, it sounds like it's yourself.

He does absolutely nothing with the company.
He was just an early round funding person.
So I own 51%, he owns 49%.
And he wouldn't like if you said this is a strategy where I Want to go.
He wouldn't try and strong arm you in a different direction or anything.
Okay, yeah.
As long as the numbers are, are good.
Yeah, we're, we're in a position now and just, just, you know, for, for your understanding.
We're in a position to where we're financially sound.
Yeah, we are stable.
We are growing.
Even though it's slow, we're growing.
We've got this new product about to launch.
We're in a very, very healthy position with long term.

Like, we realize the theory of course, is always that with technology you get to increase your multiple for sure.
Yes.
And this is still a major void.
Nothing like this exists in the space.
We've used so much experience to build this thing to kind of, you know, shape what this is going to be used for and make it very versatile for both brands and agencies.
We think that it's, it's going to be an incredible product that's going to add a lot of value to us.
So we're not in a position to give anything away.
This isn't a fire sale.

You do what would, what would make an interesting inquiry for you?
I mean, again, I, I don't call, we don't call many people.
We're not like a, you know, spray and pray.
I take the very strategic view on this because I also having worked in the industry, used to get phone calls every day.
So I get it.
But what for you would make an interesting partner?
Because I don't want to waste your time or acquirer because obviously I think your point is clear, which is you're growing, you have a product coming in the future, soon, in the very near future.

So they're, you know, again, they have a great upside and access to some key clients.

Because I don't want to get everyone on the phone for people to be like, I wasn't interested anyway.
So what, what would do you have, like, have you had offers in mind before that weren't enough?
Have you had the types of companies that you feel were or were not correct for you?
You know, for, for me, I, I think growth Potential is, is top line, making sure that we end up with the right partners.
Somebody that's not going to micromanage me once.
Once.
I mean I've driven the train this far and, and we're on a pretty good path.
So I think that would be a major thing is to make sure that whatever direction we move, it's not going to hinder our growth potential.
Make sure that we've got a good support team in place with whoever we end up merging with.
Otherwise, I mean, I should just go out and get the funding and continue running the company.
Yeah.
And just growing it bigger.
And so yeah, I would need to make sure those two things are in place.

And it's got to be enticing in terms of upfront and upfront amount to me because otherwise again, it's, if it's going to be primarily performance based payout, well then again, why wouldn't I just continue running it myself and, and letting this SAF project really get its wheels underneath it and get everything that I know it can, it can yield long term.
So if there's not an upfront payout, it's performance based.
Well, it's, it's no different than what I'm doing currently.
So it would have to be enticing in terms of a, of an upfront deal as well.
I'm not saying it's gotta be 100 upfront deal, but it's got to be enticing in terms of upfront payout.
Otherwise like I said, if it's, it's all based on performance.
Well hell, that's what I'm doing now is a performance.
Yeah, no, that makes sense.

Well we are.

Okay.

Right.

Right.
In the.

Yeah, accrued in the year.

Okay.
Yeah.

Yeah.

summary.overview:
- **Company Growth:** Projected sales for 2025 are $5.5 to $6 million, nearly double last year's $3.2 million post-contract loss.  
- **Financial Stability:** The company is debt-free, except for a small COVID loan, and expects 2024 EBITDA to reach 15-20%.  
- **Innovative Product Launch:** The new AI platform "Sentrack" aims for a January 2026 launch, focusing on sentiment analysis for social marketing.  
- **Clientele and Strategy:** Serves major brands targeting Gen Z/Gen Alpha, using a collaboration-based approach for custom influencer campaigns.  
- **Acquisition Discussions:** Open to acquisition inquiries, seeking a partner that values autonomy and provides upfront value for growth.  
- **Funding Plans:** If no acquisition occurs, intends to raise $5 million within 90 days to enhance operations and launch globally.
summary.short_summary: The company is experiencing steady, self-funded growth with projected sales of $5.5 to $6 million in 2025, nearly doubling last year's revenue of $3.2 million after a contract loss. It remains debt-free except for a small COVID loan and expects an EBITDA of 15-20% for 2024. The transition to a technology-driven SaaS model is underway with the launch of 'Sentrack', an AI sentiment analysis platform set for January 2026. The company serves major brands targeting Gen Z and Gen Alpha demographics and leverages a collaborative approach to influencer marketing. While open to acquisition discussions, the leadership seeks partners that ensure growth autonomy. If acquisition doesn't materialize, plans are in place to raise $5 million within 90 days to enhance operations and launch the SaaS product globally.
